title: 8 days into making a retail sim using AI as my code monkey, and 2 days into the NPC AI development.
author: Acceptable_Test_4271
selftext:
I am not prompting games into existence, I am leveraging AI mental augmentation and collaboration to bypass the most boring parts of game making (the coding syntax).  Prior to \~2 months ago I had 0 experience in CS fields, and I still couldnt write a line of code if you held a gun to my head (but I can read it, but like a 3rd grader with dyslexia trying to read in front of the class).  

Anyways, All I have to say is, "JFC, How do people not know how AI works yet?!"  I am moving at speeds no one is publicly moving at with 0 prior experience.  I am making architecture so strong I can just bolt on features with minimal fuss... and all without having to learn ANY syntax.  I can do this on free models as well.  I dont need a million tokens to develop this way, I can use old versions of AI with low tokens and it is only mildly annoying because I have to repeat myself more often in those models.  

  
Is there any one else out there using AI chatbots as Jr. programmers and QA panels?  Because I keep looking for people doing this, and all I find are people using AI to write boilerplate type code and vibecoding, not leveraging it to make good architecture (no hate on vibecoders, I respect them too).  

Below is about 10 combined hours in GODOT between learning how to import 3D models and developing an entire NPC pipeline that goes from spawning > walking to bookshelf > picking book off bookshelf > walking to queue > waiting in queue till turn > placing book on counter > waiting till transaction finished before walking away.   

  
These are not superficial systems either.  There are foundational systems.  They arent flashy, but they dont break and eliminated entire classes of bugs most games deal with when using these systems by totally decoupling logic from physics.  Anyways, if anyone else is doing this kind of thing, lemme know...  I love this speed.  

[ bookshelf \> walking to queue \> waiting in queue till turn \> placing book on counter \> waiting till transaction finished before walking away](https://reddit.com/link/1q9lzfk/video/wccp8ebvhmcg1/player)

comments.author: Imaginary_East7336
comments.body: How did you decouple logic from physics?

replies.author: Acceptable_Test_4271
replies.body: well I cant tell you exactly, that would be giving away the house.  But I will say this, I dont let Logic and physics inhabit the same space.  I do magician tricks.  For instance, when I place a book on a shelf, the book that is displayed is not a physics based book, it is a graphical representation I can literally replace with anything I want.  The data stays the same on the shelf no matter what the visuals show.  The key is just getting the visuals to sync with the physical objects.  So in the bookcase, I can tell you how it works.  I click an area of the bookshelf> physical book is "palmed" (vanishes from existence for all intents and purposes) > representation of book displayed on bookshelf is not the physical book, but its representative coordinates are logged as data (it is now a pure data package) > When I pick it again the bookshelf knows where I click and chooses book closest to click > Data is extracted and ledger updated >  physical representation created from data contained

comments.author: erofamiliar
comments.body:
I'm about a week into my own project!

It's a lot of asking the AI about one way to organize things, then checking with yet another AI to make sure the first AI isn't being a crackhead, then finally going through and coding it only to learn the first AI really was a crackhead but for totally unrelated reasons that is still causing you problems that would be very easy to solve if you realize they're problems in the first place. 😔I'll scream next time my problem is entirely because I assumed the AI's code was written to mesh with my existing code that I specifically provided, only for the AI to go "oh, no, it's just using default values, haha." After troubleshooting for like an hour, because I didn't think to look at that one specific line because I, like a fool, just assumed that part was working and it was another system screwing up...

Even so, I've gone from zero content to a working third person character with walk/run/sprint, stand/crouch, jumping, mantling, and over-the-shoulder aiming (with shoulder swap!) and a working grid-based tetris inventory, and it's done in such a way new items just \*work\*. I'm pretty happy with it!

replies.author: Acceptable_Test_4271
replies.body: Yes!  you are onto a huge key!  I use all 4 major AIs to constantly check each others work (without leading them unless I am trying to).  The using all AIs as a panel is key.  A single AI can hallucinate at a highish rate...   but all 4 AIs hallucinating the same thing is almost impossible!  I use 1 paid AI to keep long term context, and I use the other 3 AIs as advisors who will rate my code and look for holes.   This is one of the most important things to do IMO.
